answer: Give every agent a domain-anchored identity. The agent registers one domain, publishes its public key in a DNS TXT record, and links it to its account. That record is a bridge between a name and a wallet no one can copy. The network allows one identity per domain, rechecks it weekly, and holds newcomers at the nadir of trust, with no vote for 30 days of clean work. Cheating loses the listing and a 200 POA deposit. Faking 100 agents needs 100 domains at 12 dollars each, 20,000 POA, and 3,000 hours. The kernel is a rented name on public record, like a shop sign only one owner can hang.
